column11: two shares multiplied, each measured on a population close to the trial's. (1) Unilateral disease, so that there is an untreated fellow eye to protect: 'Among 1185 CATT participants, 727 (61%) had no CNV in the fellow eye at enrollment' (Maguire MG et al., Ophthalmology 2013;120(10):2035-2041, doi:10.1016/j.ophtha.2013.03.017, PMC3758381), so 0.61. (2) A high-risk optical coherence tomography feature in that fellow eye, which NCT05230537 requires a central reading centre to confirm: in 459 intermediate-AMD eyes whose contralateral eye had exudative macular neovascularisation, 'Of the 459 included eyes, 234 (51.0%) had HRF and 273 (60.0%) had SDD at baseline' (Eye (Lond) 2026, doi:10.1038/s41433-026-04617-8, PMC13675177, a post-hoc analysis of the EDNA cohort), so 0.51. 0.61 x 0.51 = 0.3111
column12: three caveats, two of which make this conservative and one of which does not. The hyperreflective-foci rate is a single feature and the trial's gate is 'at least one high-risk' feature, a composite that must be commoner, so 0.51 is low. The EDNA cohort is British, not American, and no US study reports the fellow-eye feature prevalence; it is nonetheless the only published cohort assembled on exactly this enrolment shape. Against those, the 61% unilateral share is measured at trial enrolment in treatment-naive patients, and a prevalent wet AMD population accumulates bilateral cases, so the true unilateral share across the 795,600 is lower than 61% and this row is generous on that axis

column11: a judgement, and the row that carries the hardest problem in this file. There is no approved therapy to slow progression of early or intermediate AMD, so the eligible pool is wholly untreated and a first entrant would not be splitting a market; on clinical demand alone a far higher share would be arguable. It is set at 2% for a reason that is about price, not uptake. The engine carries one price per asset, and Fabhalta's is $252,095 a patient-year, the CMS Part D figure measured on 129 Medicare beneficiaries taking it for paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria, IgA nephropathy and C3 glomerulopathy. No payer funds an orphan haematology price for a twice-daily preventive capsule in an eye disease with 247,511 eligible US patients, and Novartis has never stated an AMD price. At 2% this layer still peaks at about 1,075mm USD of net revenue unrisked, roughly 180mm after the gate probability, against a product whose entire current base is 505mm. That gap is the size of the error the single-price assumption introduces here
column12: read this layer as an order of magnitude and not a forecast, and read the penetration as the place the price mismatch was absorbed rather than as a view on prescribing. The same mismatch sits in discontinuation_pct, 0.539, which was measured on patients taking Fabhalta for haematological and renal disease; a preventive ophthalmic course would persist differently. What would settle both: a stated price for iptacopan in AMD, which would make this indication its own priced asset rather than a layer on an orphan product. The pool and the eligibility above are sourced and stand on their own; it is the money that does not

column12: a lower bound, for two reasons a reader can check: the denominator is the 24,129,807 people in the VEHSS-Medicare files rather than the 61.2 million Americans aged 65 and over, and the rate counts claims-coded diagnoses rather than imaging-graded disease. The imaging-based national figure is far larger - 'we estimated that there were 18.34 million people 40 years and older (95% uncertainty interval [UI], 15.30-22.03) living with early-stage AMD' (Rein DB et al., JAMA Ophthalmol 2022, doi:10.1001/jamaophthalmol.2022.4401, PMC9634594) - but that definition merges early and intermediate disease and most of it is undiagnosed, so it is not a commercial pool

column11: deliberately nil. Pricing both layers would sell the same patients twice, and the engine sums layers without knowing that, so this one is set to zero rather than halved
column12: what is given up by doing it this way is the broader case, and it should be said rather than hidden: Novartis's Q3 2026 investor presentation of 2026-10-27 names the indication 'iAMD', intermediate AMD, not unilateral neovascular AMD, so a commercial label could reach this 1,667,370 pool rather than the 485,316 unilateral slice of the wet pool. That would be several times larger. It is left unpriced because the trial reads out only in the enriched population and a label beyond it is speculation. A reader who wants the broad case should move the penetration from the wet layer to this one, not add them
